chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the kohl for the fasting person, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the kohl is such that there is no musk in it, and it has no taste in the throat, then there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Samaan ibn Mihran reports Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling that kohl does not invalidate the fast unless it possesses a distinct taste that reaches the throat, highlighting the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between mere entry into the body cavity and actual consumption. This view contrasts with some other schools that consider any substance entering the eye as breaking the fast, emphasizing the practical ease for the fasting believer while maintaining ritual purity.
